subject: maths
title: Model Question Paper 1
meta: Time: 2½ hours · Maximum marks: 85 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–17 are MCQs (1 mark each); questions 18–27 have two parts of 1 mark each; question 28 is a case study with five 1-mark questions.
Section B: questions 29–37 carry 2 marks, 38–42 carry 3 marks and 43–44 carry 5 marks.
Every answer shows the working. Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: The factors of 3x² − x − 4 are —
questions.work:
Product ac = 3 × (−4) = −12; we need two numbers with product −12 and sum −1: they are −4 and 3.
3x² − x − 4 = 3x² − 4x + 3x − 4
= x(3x − 4) + 1(3x − 4) = (3x − 4)(x + 1).

questions.q: The HCF of two numbers is 3 and their LCM is 21. If one number is 7, the other is —
questions.work:
Product of the numbers = HCF × LCM = 3 × 21 = 63.
Other number = 63 ÷ 7 = 9.

questions.q: The solution of 2x + 3y + 5 = 0 and 3x − 2y − 12 = 0 is —
questions.work:
Multiply the first by 2 and the second by 3: 4x + 6y + 10 = 0 and 9x − 6y − 36 = 0.
Add: 13x − 26 = 0 ⇒ x = 2.
Then 2(2) + 3y + 5 = 0 ⇒ 3y = −9 ⇒ y = −3.
Check: 3(2) − 2(−3) − 12 = 6 + 6 − 12 = 0 ✓.

questions.q: The roots of 2x² − 3x + 5 = 0 are —
questions.work:
D = (−3)² − 4 × 2 × 5 = 9 − 40 = −31.
D < 0, so the roots are not real.

The number of illiterate people fell from 150 lakh to 100 lakh. The percentage decrease is —
questions.work:
Decrease = 150 − 100 = 50 lakh.
Percentage decrease = 50/150 × 100 = 33⅓% (always divide by the original value).

A quadrilateral ABCD is drawn to circumscribe a circle with centre O. If ∠AOB = 125°, then ∠COD is —
questions.work:
For a quadrilateral circumscribing a circle, the angles subtended at the centre by opposite sides are supplementary: ∠AOB + ∠COD = 180°.

questions.work: For a scale factor 3/4 we mark 4 points (the larger of 3 and 4), join the 4th to C, and draw the parallel through the 3rd.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, match the columns or true/false).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) If a = 6 and d = 5, the 11th term is ____. (ii) The sum of the first ten terms of 7, 14, 21, 28, … is ____.
Write True or False: (i) A number increased by 20% and then decreased by 20% returns to itself. (ii) 0.2% = 0.002.
questions.answer:
(i) False: 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96, a net decrease of 4%.
(ii) True: 0.2/100 = 0.002.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Under an instalment plan, the part paid at the time of purchase is the ____. (ii) Interest charged = sum of instalments − ____.
questions.answer:
(i) cash down payment.
(ii) balance (= cash price − cash down), because the instalments repay the balance plus interest.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠DAB = 110°, so ∠BCD = ____. (ii) AB is a chord of a circle with centre O, ∠OAB = 40° and C is on the major arc; ∠ACB = ____.
questions.answer:
(i) Opposite angles are supplementary: 180° − 110° = 70°.
(ii) OA = OB, so ∠OBA = 40° and ∠AOB = 180° − 80° = 100°; ∠ACB = ½ × 100° = 50°.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks (any two): (i) Common tangents to two non-intersecting circles ____ (ii) Tangents at a point on the circle ____ (iii) Tangents at the ends of a diameter are ____ (iv) Common tangents to two intersecting circles ____.
questions.answer: (i) 4. (ii) one. (iii) parallel (both are perpendicular to the same diameter). (iv) 2.

questions.q: Write True or False: (i) △ABC with BC = 3 cm, ∠C = 30° and AB − AC = 3.2 cm can be constructed. (ii) For the perpendicular bisector of AB, the compass must be opened to less than ½AB.
questions.answer:
(i) False: we need AB − AC < BC, but 3.2 > 3.
(ii) False: the radius must be more than ½AB so that the arcs from A and B meet.

questions.q: Match: (i) If P(−1, 1) is the midpoint of A(−3, b) and B(1, b + 4), b = ____ (ii) The perimeter of the triangle with vertices (0, 4), (0, 0), (3, 0) is ____ — (A) −1 (B) 12 (C) 1 (D) 7
Fill in the blanks: (i) The hour hand of a clock turns through ____ in 30 minutes. (ii) The area swept by a 10 cm minute hand in 20 minutes is ____.
questions.answer:
(i) The hour hand turns 30° per hour, so 15° in 30 minutes.
(ii) 20 minutes = 120° = ⅓ of a turn: ⅓ × 22/7 × 10² = 2200/21 ≈ 104.76 cm².

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) A hemisphere whose volume and curved surface area are numerically equal has diameter ____. (ii) A cylindrical tank of capacity 6160 cm³ and diameter 28 cm has depth ____.
questions.answer:
(i) (2/3)πr³ = 2πr² ⇒ r = 3, so the diameter is 6 units.
(ii) r = 14: 22/7 × 196 × h = 6160 ⇒ 616h = 6160 ⇒ h = 10 cm.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: (ii) sec θ(1 − sin θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = ____. Also, (i) cos 47° cot 79° − sin 43° tan 11° = ____.
questions.answer:
(ii) sec θ(1 − sin θ) = sec θ − tan θ; (sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = sec²θ − tan²θ = 1.
(i) cos 47° = sin 43° and cot 79° = tan 11°, so the two terms are equal: 0.

sections.passage: A school garden is a square of side (x + 5) m. A square flower bed of side (x − 5) m is made in one corner and the rest is grass. The gardener also stacks cube-shaped boxes of side (x + 1) m.

questions.q: A table is available for ₹1,700 cash or ₹500 down and ₹1,400 after 2 months. Find the rate of interest charged.
O is the centre of a circle, ∠SOQ = 150° and P, R are on the circle so that PQRS is cyclic with P on the minor arc QS. Find x = ∠SRQ and y = ∠SPQ.
questions.answer:
x = ½∠SOQ = ½ × 150° = 75° (angle on the major arc).
PQRS is cyclic: y = 180° − x = 105°.

questions.q: PA and PB are tangents to a circle with PA = 14 cm. A third tangent CD touches the circle at E, with C on PA and D on PB. Find the perimeter of △PCD.
questions.answer:
CE = CA and DE = DB (tangents from C and from D).
Perimeter = PC + CD + PD = PC + CE + ED + PD = (PC + CA) + (DB + PD) = PA + PB = 14 + 14 = 28 cm.

questions.q: Write the steps of construction of tangents to a circle of radius 3 cm from a point P 6 cm from its centre O.
questions.answer:
1. Draw a circle of radius 3 cm with centre O.
2. Mark P with OP = 6 cm and join OP.
3. Draw the perpendicular bisector of OP; let it cut OP at M (OM = 3 cm).
4. With centre M and radius MO draw a circle cutting the given circle at Q and R.
5. Join PQ and PR — these are the tangents.
6. Check: PQ = √(6² − 3²) = √27 ≈ 5.2 cm.

questions.q: A farmer buys a circular field at ₹700 per m² for ₹4,31,200. Find the perimeter of the field.
The radii of two cylinders are in the ratio 2 : 3 and their heights in the ratio 5 : 3. Find the ratio of their volumes.
Prove that cos⁴A − sin⁴A = 1 − 2 sin²A.
questions.answer: cos⁴A − sin⁴A = (cos²A − sin²A)(cos²A + sin²A) = cos²A − sin²A = (1 − sin²A) − sin²A = 1 − 2 sin²A.

questions.q: If cos(40° + 2x) = sin 30°, where 40° + 2x is acute, find x.
The sum of the digits of a two-digit number is 13 and the sum of their squares is 89. Find the number.
questions.answer:
Let the digits be a and b: a + b = 13, a² + b² = 89.
(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab ⇒ 169 = 89 + 2ab ⇒ ab = 40.
b = 13 − a: a(13 − a) = 40 ⇒ a² − 13a + 40 = 0 ⇒ (a − 5)(a − 8) = 0.
The digits are 8 and 5; the number is 85 or 58.

questions.q: A cooler costs ₹6,000 cash or ₹2,000 down and two equal monthly instalments. If interest is 12% per annum (simple), find each instalment.
Find the value of m if the points (3, 1), (−2, −3) and (8, 2m) are collinear.
Prove that tan θ + cot θ = sec θ cosec θ.
questions.answer: tan θ + cot θ = sin θ/cos θ + cos θ/sin θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = 1/(sin θ cos θ) = sec θ cosec θ.

questions.q: A bag contains 25 cards numbered 1 to 25. Find the probability that the number drawn is (i) divisible by 3 or 5 (ii) a perfect square.
The shadow of a tower is 10 m longer when the sun's elevation is 30° than when it is 45°. Find the height of the tower. (√3 = 1.732)
questions.answer:
Let the height be h. Shadow at 45° = h; at 30° = h√3.
h√3 − h = 10 ⇒ h = 10/(√3 − 1) = 10/0.732 ≈ 13.66 m.

or.q: An aeroplane 3000 m high passes vertically above another at an instant when their elevations from a point on the ground are 60° and 45°. Find the vertical distance between them.
or.answer:
Horizontal distance d: tan 60° = 3000/d ⇒ d = 3000/√3 = 1000√3 = 1732 m.
Lower plane: height = d tan 45° = 1732 m.
Vertical distance = 3000 − 1732 = 1268 m.
